clinical.citation: ASHG 2017 - Debunking the cerebral palsy (CP)-birth asphyxia myth: Frequent genomic etiologies for CP identified by exome sequencing (Moreno-De-Luca et al.)

variants.description: Rare loss-of-function variant in MAP3K12 (specific nucleotide/protein change not provided in abstract)
phenotypes: Cerebral palsy

clinical.diagnostic_reason: Rare LoF variant absent from population databases (ExAC, EVS, 1000G); MAP3K12 predicted to be extremely LoF intolerant; proposed as a novel CP candidate gene

clinical.citation: Prioritizing de novo potential non-canonical splicing variants in neurodevelopmental disorders (PMID: 38113761)

variants.description: MAP3K12 c.436G>A (chr12:53880317 C>T), missense; non-canonical splicing variant causing exon 4 91bp deletion in minigene assay
phenotypes: Neurodevelopmental disorder (unspecified developmental delay/NDD)

clinical.diagnostic_reason: De novo variant in a patient with NDD; minigene assay showed abnormal splicing (exon 4 91bp deletion); MAP3K12 implicated in axon growth

model_organism.citation: Xenopus Dlk study - Dual leucine zipper kinase is necessary for retinal ganglion cell axonal regeneration in Xenopus laevis (PMID: 37152673)
model_organism.knockout_type: other (CRISPR/Cas9 F0 mosaic knockout/knockdown of map3k12 injected at the one-cell stage)
phenotypes: map3k12/Dlk is necessary for RGC axonal regeneration after optic nerve crush, in a dose-dependent manner
Loss of Dlk does not affect RGC innervation of the brain during development
Loss of Dlk does not affect visually driven behavior
Loss of Dlk blocks axonal regeneration and functional vision restoration after optic nerve crush
Loss of Dlk does not alter acute mitochondrial movement in RGC axons after crush
Loss of Dlk blocks Jun phosphorylation and nuclear translocation in RGCs days after crush
Jun is dispensable for reinnervation

model_organism.citation: Dual leucine zipper kinase is required for mechanical allodynia and microgliosis after nerve injury (PMID: 29968565)
phenotypes: Genetic or pharmacological inhibition of DLK reduces mechanical hypersensitivity (allodynia) in a neuropathic pain model
DLK inhibition prevents spinal cord microgliosis after nerve injury
DLK controls a transcriptional program in somatosensory neurons, including Csf1 and other pain-related genes

model_organism.citation: DLK signaling in axotomized neurons triggers complement activation and loss of upstream synapses (PMID: 38363678)
phenotypes: DLK signaling in injured motoneurons triggers induction of phagocytic microglia and synapse loss
DLK regulates C1q expression, first in the axotomized motoneuron and later in microglia
Microglia phagocytose presynaptic components of upstream synapses
Loss of cholinergic C boutons from axotomized motoneurons depends on DLK and on microglia

model_organism.citation: Promoting regeneration while blocking cell death preserves motor neuron function in a model of ALS (PMID: 36342754)
model_organism.knockout_type: conditional knockout (DLK deletion combined with constitutive ATF3 expression in SOD1G93A mice)
phenotypes: DLK deletion plus ATF3 expression gives synergistic protection in the SOD1G93A ALS model
Fewer motor neurons undergo cell death
Reduced axon degeneration
Preserved motor function and neuromuscular connectivity
Improved motor neuron electrophysiology, histology and behavior

model_organism.citation: Translatome analysis reveals cellular network in DLK-dependent hippocampal glutamatergic neuron degeneration (PMID: 40067879)
phenotypes: DLK-dependent translatome identified in hippocampal glutamatergic neurons
Dorsal CA1 and dentate gyrus neurons are vulnerable to elevated DLK expression, while CA3 neurons are less vulnerable
Increased DLK signaling is associated with microtubule disruption, potentially via STMN4
Altered neurite outgrowth, axon specification and synapse formation in cultured hippocampal neurons with different DLK levels

model_organism.citation: Dual Leucine Zipper Kinase Is Constitutively Active in the Adult Mouse Brain and Has Both Stress-Induced and Homeostatic Functions (PMID: 32659913)
model_organism.knockout_type: other (pharmacological DLK inhibition; rTg4510 tauopathy model)
phenotypes: DLK constitutively drives nuclear p-c-Jun in cerebellar granule neurons
In rTg4510 forebrain, p-c-Jun accumulation is DLK-dependent and correlates with synaptic loss and gliosis
DLK inhibition reduces a core set of JNK-pathway transcripts
In the cerebellum, DLK regulates IGF1 signaling through IGFBP5 induction

biological.citation: Sun et al. 2026 - ATF2 phosphorylation is a core transcriptional driver of neuron apoptosis (PMID: 42161275)
biological.summary: A genome-wide CRISPR inhibition screen in human neurons identified DLK/MAP3K12, JUN and ATF2 as a pro-death cascade. MAP3 kinase phosphorylation of ATF2 drives upregulation of JUN and neuronal apoptosis. Interfering with ATF2 prevents neuronal apoptosis in vitro and in vivo.

biological.citation: Kim et al. 2022 - FK506-binding protein-like and FK506-binding protein 8 regulate dual leucine zipper kinase degradation and neuronal responses to axon injury (PMID: 35101451)
biological.summary: A yeast two-hybrid screen identified FKBPL as a DLK-binding protein. FKBPL binds the DLK kinase domain, inhibits its kinase activity and induces ubiquitin-dependent degradation. FKBP8 also promotes DLK degradation via autophagy and proteasome, with K271 as the ubiquitination/SUMO3 site. FKBP8 overexpression delays axon degeneration and neuronal death after axotomy in vivo.

biological.citation: Shin et al. 2022 - A Critical Role for DLK and LZK in Axonal Repair in the Mammalian Spinal Cord (PMID: 35361703)
biological.summary: In mice, inducible neuronal deletion of both DLK (MAP3K12) and LZK (MAP3K13), but not either alone, abolished PTEN deletion-induced regeneration and sprouting of corticospinal tract axons. The two kinases are redundant and act in both injured and uninjured neurons, independently of PTEN/mTOR signaling.

biological.citation: Bhattacharyya et al. 2024 - DLK signaling in axotomized neurons triggers complement activation and loss of upstream synapses (PMID: 38363678)
biological.summary: In conditional knockout mice, DLK/MAP3K12 activation in axotomized motoneurons triggers C1q expression, first in the neuron and later in microglia, along with phagocytic microglia and loss of upstream synapses. DLK is therefore a neuronal driver of injury-induced inflammation.

biological.citation: Pozniak/Wang et al. 2018 - Dual leucine zipper kinase is required for mechanical allodynia and microgliosis after nerve injury (PMID: 29968565)
biological.summary: Genetic or pharmacological inhibition of DLK (Map3k12) reduces mechanical hypersensitivity and spinal microgliosis after nerve injury in mice. DLK controls a transcriptional program in somatosensory neurons that includes pain-related genes such as Csf1.

biological.citation: Patel et al. 2015 - Discovery of dual leucine zipper kinase (DLK, MAP3K12) inhibitors with activity in neurodegeneration models (PMID: 25341110)
biological.summary: The selective, brain-penetrant DLK inhibitor GNE-3511 protected neurons from degeneration in vitro. It was also active in two animal models of neurodegeneration, supporting DLK kinase activity as a driver of neuronal degeneration.

biological.citation: Wang et al. 2021 - MiR-191-5p alleviates microglial cell injury by targeting Map3k12 to inhibit the MAPK signaling pathway in Alzheimer's disease (PMID: 34818971)
biological.summary: miR-191-5p directly targets the Map3k12 3'UTR (shown by luciferase assay) and downregulates its expression. In Aβ1-42-treated microglia and APP/PS1 mice, this inhibits MAPK signaling and reduces microglial injury and apoptosis. Map3k12 therefore promotes MAPK signaling and injury in AD models.

biological.citation: Li et al. 2015 - MicroRNA-130a Targets MAP3K12 to Modulate Diabetic Endothelial Progenitor Cell Function (PMID: 25999017)
biological.summary: MAP3K12 is a target of miR-130a in endothelial progenitor cells. Reduced miR-130a in diabetic EPCs and high glucose lead to sustained JNK activation, apoptosis and dysfunction through MAP3K12.

biological.citation: Tang et al. 2024 - Comprehensive analysis of MAPK genes in the prognosis, immune characteristics, and drug treatment of renal clear cell carcinoma (PMID: 39038636)
biological.summary: MAP3K12 was the most significant gene in a six-gene MAPK prognostic signature in ccRCC and had independent prognostic value. Knockout and overexpression experiments in vitro and in vivo showed it promotes RCC proliferation, migration, invasion and tumour progression.

biological.citation: Wang et al. 2021 - Celastrol attenuates ischemia/reperfusion-mediated memory dysfunction by downregulating AK005401/MAP3K12 (PMID: 33387968)
biological.summary: Ischemia/reperfusion in mice and OGD/R in HT-22 hippocampal cells upregulated lncRNA AK005401 and MAP3K12, with increased p-JNK/p-c-Jun and reduced PI3K/Akt activity, leading to mitochondrial dysfunction and apoptosis. Celastrol downregulated AK005401/MAP3K12 and improved memory.
